lastCompletedStory.title: Wait a settle window before the delivery-verification capture

nextStoryContext: sendKeysVerified (src/tmux/dispatch.ts) now sleeps a new exported constant SEND_KEYS_SETTLE_MS (50ms) via the injected sleepFn between every send-keys spawn and its isComposerEmptied verify capture, on every attempt (not just the first). This fixes attempt-1 misreporting an undelivered payload as delivered when capture-pane still shows the pre-send screen. isComposerEmptied itself, the send-keys argv shape (text + 'Enter' in one call, no -l), and the idle-gate poll logic are all untouched. A new test in the 'sendKeysVerified' describe block proves the settle window is honored via a staged capturePaneFn (returns PRE-send screen until the injected sleepFn is called with exactly SEND_KEYS_SETTLE_MS, then POST-send screen). One pre-existing test ('sends keys immediately when pane is idle on first check') was updated: it previously asserted sleepCount===0 when the idle-gate needed no poll, but now the unconditional settle sleep always fires once per attempt, so it now asserts sleeps toEqual([SEND_KEYS_SETTLE_MS]). Any future work touching sendKeysVerified's retry/backoff timing should account for this settle sleep firing on every attempt (not just failed ones) when reasoning about sleepFn call counts in tests.

officialDocsValidated.summary: tmux's man page documents capture-pane/send-keys semantics but does not specify a render-refresh SLA; corroborating community reports (e.g. tmux-python/libtmux#188) confirm capture-pane immediately after send-keys can observe stale (pre-send) content, matching this story's premise. No official API changed; the fix is a client-side settle sleep, which is the documented workaround pattern.
